scenes.text: The first humans ever to fly rode a hot air balloon over Paris, in seventeen eighty-three.
Its makers, Joseph and Etienne Montgolfier, came from a family of paper makers in France.
Their balloons rose by burning straw, wool, and sometimes even old shoes.
Before risking people, they sent up a very unusual test crew.
A sheep, a duck and a rooster took off from the palace of Versailles.
King Louis the sixteenth and Marie Antoinette watched them fly for about eight minutes.
The animals landed around two miles from the palace.
Next it was time for humans, and the king wanted to send prisoners.
Instead, a young scientist named Pilatre de Rozier volunteered, with the Marquis d'Arlandes.
On November twenty-first, the two men lifted off and drifted over Paris.
They stayed up for about twenty-five minutes and travelled around five miles.
Benjamin Franklin, then in Paris, witnessed the balloon flights.
It was risky, because sparks from the fire could set the balloon alight.
Would you have volunteered for the first flight?

title: The first humans to fly used a hot air balloon 🎈
caption: On Nov 21, 1783, two men flew over Paris for about 25 minutes in a Montgolfier hot air balloon. The test pilots before them? A sheep, a duck and a rooster.
